section_summary.extract_value: This Results section presents findings from a single study comparing US and non-US samples (total N=9,665 based on degrees of freedom). The study tested a structural equation model examining relationships between age, education, BMI, body appreciation, body dissatisfaction, and subjective happiness. US participants were significantly older and had higher BMIs than non-US participants, while non-US participants had higher educational levels. The modified model showed excellent fit across both samples, with body appreciation showing a strong positive association with subjective happiness, and BMI having both direct negative and indirect effects on subjective happiness through body appreciation.

section_summary.extract_value: This Results section presents findings from a single study with two samples (US and non-US, N=9,665 total). The study tested a path model examining relationships between education, age, BMI, body appreciation (BA), body dissatisfaction (BD), and subjective happiness (SH). US participants were significantly older and had higher BMIs than non-US participants, while non-US participants had higher educational levels. The final constrained multi-group model (Fig. 2) showed nearly identical standardized path coefficients across both samples, with BMI showing a negative path to body appreciation (-.24 for US, -.21 for non-US) and body appreciation showing a strong positive association with subjective happiness.
